recipes.name: Cottage pie
recipes.method_note: The mash goes on hot mince, so it sits on top rather than sinking.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 200C.
Peel {{ing:potato-large}} and cut into rough chunks.
Put them in a pan of cold water. Bring to the boil.
Cook 18 minutes, until a knife slides in with no resistance.
Chop {{ing:onion-medium}} and {{ing:carrot-medium}} small.
Put a large pan on a medium heat. Add {{ing:vegetable-oil}}.
Add the onion and carrot. Cook 8 minutes, until soft.
Add {{ing:beef-mince-20-fat}}. Break it up with a spoon.
Cook 8 minutes, until no pink is left.
Add {{ing:chopped-tomatoes-tinned}}, {{ing:stock-chicken}} and {{ing:worcestershire-sauce}}.
Simmer 20 minutes, until thick enough to hold a spoon mark.
Drain the potatoes. Add {{ing:butter-block}} and {{ing:milk-semi-skimmed}}.
Mash until smooth.
Tip the mince into an oven dish. Spread the mash over the top.
steps.note: Work from the edges inwards so the mash does not sink.

steps.instruction: Bake 25 minutes, until the top is browned in patches.

recipes.name: Toad in the hole
recipes.method_note: Do not open the oven while it rises. It will drop and not come back.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 220C.
Put {{ing:flour-plain}} and {{ing:salt}} in a bowl.
Crack in {{ing:egg-medium}}. Whisk to a thick paste.
Add {{ing:milk-semi-skimmed}} slowly, whisking, until smooth.
steps.note: Lumps come from adding the milk all at once.

steps.instruction: Rest the batter 30 minutes.
Put {{ing:vegetable-oil}} in a roasting tin. Add {{ing:sausage-pork}}.
Roast 15 minutes, until the sausages are browned and the oil is smoking.
Take the tin out. Pour the batter around the sausages.
steps.note: It should hiss. That is what makes it rise.

steps.instruction: Put it straight back in. Bake 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 200C.
Peel {{ing:potato-large}} and cut into chunks. Boil 18 minutes.
Put {{ing:cod-fillet}} and {{ing:salmon-fillet}} in a wide pan.
Pour {{ing:milk-whole}} over. Bring to a bare simmer.
Cook 5 minutes, until the fish flakes with a fork.
Lift the fish out. Keep the milk.
Melt {{ing:butter-block}} in a clean pan.
Stir in {{ing:flour-plain}}. Cook 2 minutes.
steps.note: It should look like wet sand.

steps.instruction: Add the fishy milk a splash at a time, whisking, until smooth.
steps.note: Adding it slowly is what stops lumps.

steps.instruction: Cook 5 minutes, until it coats the back of a spoon.
Chop {{ing:fresh-parsley}} and stir it in.
Break the fish into large pieces in an oven dish.
Pour the sauce over.
Drain and mash the potatoes. Spread over the top.
Grate {{ing:cheddar-cheese}} over. Bake 25 minutes.
Slice {{ing:leek}} into rounds. Rinse them in a colander.
Peel and chop {{ing:potato-medium}} and {{ing:onion-medium}}.
Melt {{ing:butter-block}} in a large pan on a low heat.
Add the leeks and onion. Cook 10 minutes, until soft but not coloured.
Add the potatoes and {{ing:stock-vegetable}}.
Simmer 20 minutes, until the potato falls apart when pressed.
Blend until smooth.
steps.note: If using a stick blender, take the pan off the heat first.

steps.instruction: Stir in {{ing:double-cream}}.

recipes.name: Sausages, beans and chips
recipes.method_note: A whole meal from the freezer and a tin. No apology needed.

steps.instruction: Heat the oven to 220C.
Cut {{ing:potato-large}} into chips, skin on.
Toss the chips with {{ing:vegetable-oil}} on a baking tray.
Spread them out so they are not touching.
steps.note: Piled chips steam instead of crisping.

steps.instruction: Bake 30 minutes, turning once halfway.
Put {{ing:sausage-pork}} on a second tray. Add them to the oven after 10 minutes.
Heat {{ing:baked-beans}} in a small pan for 5 minutes.
Check the sausages are browned all over before serving.
